symptom: `alter workflow` leaving a user task with one outcome that holds activities (dropping its other outcome, or inserting such a task) passed `check -p` and `exec`; mx check 11.14.0 then CE1876 "Single outcome must not contain any activities in its flow." — while `create workflow` refused the same shape as MDL-WF02
cause: ValidateAlterWorkflow skipped WF02 deliberately because a later op can still add the second outcome, so no alter was ever judged — a correct concern answered by not checking at all
insight: When a per-statement rule is skipped because 'a later op may repair it', the fix is to move the rule to the scope where the repair is visible — a script-level replay over a small model of the affected state — not to keep skipping it. Baseline preference: the script's own CREATE (makes it decidable without -p, so the corpus can carry a .fail.mdl), then the stored document, then nothing (only inserted tasks known → a stored-task drop stays silent). Every op the model cannot follow (@N, an unresolved ref that may be a builder-generated name, an ambiguous name) marks the task unknown rather than guessing; that keeps the expensive direction (a false refusal now blocks exec) closed. Measured on 11.14.0 with two copies: drop -> CE1876; drop then `insert into Review { outcomes 'Escalate' { } }` in a later statement -> 0 errors.
